blocks.passage:
FX risk is the silent partner in every international deal. It sits in the background while the deal is negotiated, and then decides, at the moment of payment, whether the margin you thought you had really exists. For a company that has been running on 5% margins, a 3% move in the exchange rate wipes out most of a year's work.

Managing FX risk starts with measuring it. Which currencies do you receive, and when? Which do you pay, and when? Once you can see the exposure on a single page, you can start to choose: natural hedges (matching inflows and outflows), forwards (locking in today's rate for a future date), or, in some cases, simply accepting the risk and pricing it in.

The worst strategy is no strategy.

audio.text:
Let me draw this on the whiteboard, because once you see the exposure on one page, the risk becomes obvious.

On this side, what comes in. You've been selling to Europe, so you're receiving euros — a big chunk every month. On the other side, what goes out. You've been buying most of your inputs in dollars, and paying salaries in reais.

Now here's where the real risk lives. You receive euros but you pay dollars, and those two currencies move independently. So your margin isn't really a margin — it's a bet on the euro-dollar rate, whether you meant it to be or not.

You've got three choices. One, a natural hedge: find some dollar income to match the dollar costs. Two, a forward: lock in today's euro-dollar rate for your big payments over the next six months, so you know exactly what your margin is. Three, accept the risk but price a buffer into your quotes.

For a company running on thin margins like yours, I'd lock in the big ones with forwards. You've been leaving your whole year's profit exposed to a chart you don't control.

items.q: "Our **FX risk** is significant." FX risk is…
items.why: FX risk = risco cambial.

items.q: To **hedge** means to…
options: protect against a risk, e.g. currency movement
items.why: To hedge = proteger-se de um risco.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A **forward contract** lets you **___** today's rate for the future."
items.why: Lock in = travar a taxa.

items.q: "The currency has high **volatility**." Volatility means…
items.why: Volatility = volatilidade.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The **spot rate** is the rate for…"
items.why: Spot rate = taxa à vista (para hoje).

items.q: "Your margin is really a **bet** on the exchange rate." To be a bet on something means to…
items.why: A bet on = uma aposta em algo incerto.

items.q: "You've been **leaving it exposed**." To leave something exposed means to…
items.why: Leave exposed = deixar sem proteção.

items.q: "Let's **lock in** the rate now." To lock in means to…
items.why: Lock in = travar, fixar.

items.q: "A rate move could **wipe out** the margin." To wipe out means to…
items.why: Wipe out = eliminar por completo.

items.q: "Let's **price in** a buffer for currency swings." To price in means to…
options: include a cost in the price you quote
items.why: Price in = embutir no preço.
